name: Wooden Chair
tagline: Dynamic flexural strength, shock absorption & tenon joint security
description: All-purpose wooden chairs require high flexural strength (MOR) to handle continuous shifting body weight, backward tilting, and point-load stresses on leg tenons.

structuralDemands.loadType: Dynamic cyclic cantilever weight (150–180 kg)
structuralDemands.criticalZone: Rear leg-to-seat side rail joint (maximum bending moment)
structuralDemands.recommendedCut: Rift or Quarter-sawn for legs (zero twist)

rules: Grain Direction: Always run grain vertically through legs to resist axial compression and avoid tenon shrinkage.
Joinery Selection: Prioritize traditional mortise-and-tenon or loose tenons (min 12 mm thick). Avoid pocket screws on leg joints.
Glue Choice: Type II cross-linking PVA for indoor chairs; polyurethane or epoxy for outdoor/bentwood parts.
Moisture Control: Acclimate timber to 8%–10% moisture content for at least 72 hours before cutting mortises.
